# AWS Fault Injection Service

Store experiment templates and execute aws:fis:wait actions locally with durable wall-clock state, dependencies, and alarm stop conditions.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `fis` |
| Signing name | `fis` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2020-12-01` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Real local wait actions; all other fault actions unsupported |
| Selected operations | 16 of 26 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-fault-injection-service) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- The full AWS action catalog is unsupported: EC2, EBS, ECS, EKS, RDS, network, SSM, CloudWatch, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Kinesis, Lambda, S3, ARC and every action other than aws:fis:wait. Unsupported action IDs fail validation by name; no infrastructure fault effects are simulated.
- ListTargetResourceTypes returns an empty list and GetTargetResourceType returns ResourceNotFoundException because wait has no targets. Stored template targets are not resolved, sampled or modified.
- Experiment target account configurations, multi-account experiments, experiment options, safety levers, experiment reports and ListExperimentResolvedTargets are not whitelisted.
- Log configuration is stored and destination existence is validated; no experiment logs are emitted to CloudWatch Logs or S3.
- Worker steps are polled every 100 milliseconds; downtime counts toward an already-running wait. Alarm lookups occur before each transactional step, so changes are observed on the next poll.
- Role existence is validated, but role assumption, IAM trust-policy evaluation and remote AWS calls are not performed. Client-token replay is scoped to retained resource records.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.

## Supported operations

The table is generated from the profile and pinned Smithy model. Routes show REST bindings or the standard
JSON/Query endpoint. RPC v2 CBOR uses its service/operation route, as described in
[protocol handling](../architecture/request-flow.md). Supported members are selected separately in the
[shape whitelist](https://github.com/amjadjibon/tinystack/blob/main/generator/model/profile.json); an enabled operation may reject unsupported options.

| Operation | HTTP binding |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateExperimentTemplate` | `POST /experimentTemplates` |
| `DeleteExperimentTemplate` | `DELETE /experimentTemplates/{id}` |
| `GetAction` | `GET /actions/{id}` |
| `GetExperiment` | `GET /experiments/{id}` |
| `GetExperimentTemplate` | `GET /experimentTemplates/{id}` |
| `GetTargetResourceType` | `GET /targetResourceTypes/{resourceType}` |
| `ListActions` | `GET /actions` |
| `ListExperimentTemplates` | `GET /experimentTemplates` |
| `ListExperiments` | `GET /experiments` |
| `ListTagsForResource` | `GET /tags/{resourceArn}` |
| `ListTargetResourceTypes` | `GET /targetResourceTypes` |
| `StartExperiment` | `POST /experiments` |
| `StopExperiment` | `DELETE /experiments/{id}` |
| `TagResource` | `POST /tags/{resourceArn}` |
